Validate annual livestock consumption against cohort exposure.

Source: R/livestock_water_annual.R
as_annual_livestock_water.Rd

Adapt extensive direct-water quantities to an annual consumption ledger, matching an independently supplied cohort inventory before any aggregation. Drinking requirements and free drinking intake remain distinct from net consumptive blue water. FAO (2019), Water use of livestock production systems and supply chains, sections 4.5.4–4.5.5, distinguishes supplied, returned and evaporated water (ISBN 978-92-5-131713-6). No return fraction, animal-day exposure, year or territory is inferred by this adapter.

Source and inventory scope declarations are attestations, not proof of applicability or completeness. The inventory must enumerate all cohorts for the stated target scope independently of rate availability. Annual snapshot heads are not automatically annual animal-days. This function preserves canonical identities and does not aggregate compatibility buckets.

Usage

as_annual_livestock_water(ledger, inventory, coverage = c("abort", "partial"))

Arguments

ledger

Tibble of extensive water quantities, for example from calculate_livestock_water(). It must carry the inventory matching columns below, quantity_basis, consumption_m3, coverage_direct_water, consumption_source, consumption_basis, water_origin, consumption_boundary and boundary_source. Eligible quantities have complete drinking/service coverage, known nonnegative consumption, water_origin = "surface_or_groundwater", and consumption_boundary = "net_freshwater_consumption", describing withdrawals less returns to the same relevant freshwater system and assessment interval. A directly supplied "net_consumptive_blue_water" quantity requires its own consumption provenance. A "withdrawal" ledger additionally requires drinking/service volumes and explicit fractions, whose calculation must match the supplied consumption. Requirement and intake rows can be retained under partial coverage but never become consumptive water. Unknown metadata may be supplied as NA.

inventory

Tibble unique by exposure_id, with year, canonical reporting_polity_code, item_cbs_code, cohort, production_system, animal_days, period_start, period_end, inventory_source, and inventory_scope. Dates must be Date vectors within the single declared calendar year. Each ledger ID must match these identity/exposure columns exactly; missing ledger IDs remain visible as missing exposure. Inventory metadata are retained in the exposure_inventory attribute.

coverage

"abort" requires eligible quantities for every inventory row. "partial" warns and retains all inventory rows, with unknown impact_u for uncovered rows. It does not declare a complete footprint.

Value

A tibble retaining ledger fields and inventory identities, with coverage_status, impact_u (eligible consumptive cubic metres only), impact_quantity_basis, method_livestock_water and polity_year_basis. The source ledger and independent inventory are retained as attributes, excluding the unrelated derived CBS extract cache (.cb_extracts). Source provenance columns and other attributes are preserved. Structural mismatches and invalid annual scope always abort, even under partial coverage.

Examples

# Entirely illustrative quantities, not observed farm data.
identity <- tibble::tibble(year = 2000L, area_code = 203L) |>
  add_polity_code()
inventory <- tibble::tibble(
  exposure_id = "illustrative", year = 2000L,
  reporting_polity_code = identity$polity_code, item_cbs_code = 960L,
  cohort = "lactating", production_system = "illustrative",
  animal_days = 100, period_start = as.Date("2000-01-01"),
  period_end = as.Date("2000-12-31"), inventory_source = "Toy inventory",
  inventory_scope = "Toy herd with one cohort"
)
ledger <- dplyr::mutate(
  inventory, quantity_basis = "net_consumptive_blue_water",
  consumption_m3 = 3, coverage_direct_water = "complete",
  consumption_source = "Toy water balance", consumption_basis = "assumed",
  water_origin = "surface_or_groundwater",
  consumption_boundary = "net_freshwater_consumption",
  boundary_source = "Toy matched supply and returns"
)
as_annual_livestock_water(ledger, inventory)
